summary: The study investigates the use of thermally grown GeO2 as a passivation layer for high-k gate dielectric layers deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD). The research focuses on the intermixing behavior of GeO2 with high-k materials like ZrO2, HfO2, and Al2O3 during ALD and the electrical passivation of the Ge/GeOx interface. The results show that GeO2 can effectively passivate the interface, leading to low interface state densities and good capacitance-voltage characteristics.
evidence: ZrO2, HfO2, and Al2O3 were deposited by atomic layer deposition. GeO2 and ZrO2 or HfO2 intermix during ALD, together with partial reduction of Ge4+. Almost no intermixing or reduction occurs during Al2O3 ALD. Capacitors show well-behaved capacitance-voltage characteristics on both n- and p-Ge, indicating efficient passivation of the Ge/GeOx interface.
